question: What percentage of the total catchment area of the Krishna basin flows through Karnataka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Krishna River basin is one of the major river basins in India and spans over multiple states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Karnataka holds a significant portion of the Krishna River basin’s catchment area.
 
• Approximately 44% of the Krishna basin’s total catchment area flows through the state of Karnataka.
 
• This percentage signifies the importance of Karnataka in terms of the Krishna River’s water resources and its utilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna River:**

 
 
• The Krishna River is one of the longest rivers in India, originating in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
 
• It flows through the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The river is approximately 1,400 kilometers long and plays a crucial role in the irrigation and water supply for these states.
 
 
 
• **Catchment Area:**
 
 
• The catchment area of a river is the region from which all the precipitation flows to the river.
 
• It is also known as a drainage basin or watershed.
 
• The size and characteristics of the catchment area influence the volume and flow rate of the river.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Krishna River Basin:**
 
 
• The basin supports a large population with its water resources being used for drinking, irrigation, and industrial purposes.
 
• Agriculture in the Krishna basin is heavily dependent on the river, making it a lifeline for millions of farmers.
 
• It also has several important dams and reservoirs like the Almatti Dam, Srisailam Dam, and Nagarjuna Sagar Dam.
 
 
 
• **Water Sharing Disputes:**
 
 
• Due to its extensive use and importance, the Krishna River has been a subject of water sharing disputes among the states it flows through.
 
• The Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal has been constituted multiple times to adjudicate and allocate water sharing among the states.
